alt.en: The front of a dark red church with a white classical portico: four tall fluted columns with Corinthian capitals carry a pediment edged with carved dentils. A plaque between the columns reads "HANSON PLACE S.D.A CHURCH CONSTRUCTED 1860". Arched stained-glass windows stand at both sides; below are the tops of three wooden doorways, with Christmas wreaths on the column bases, and the bare branches of a tree at the right.
alt.es: La fachada de una iglesia rojo oscuro con un pórtico clásico blanco: cuatro columnas altas acanaladas, con capiteles corintios, sostienen un frontón con dentículos tallados. Una placa entre las columnas dice "HANSON PLACE S.D.A CHURCH CONSTRUCTED 1860". A los lados hay ventanas de vidriera en arco; abajo se ve la parte alta de tres puertas de madera, con coronas navideñas al pie de las columnas, y a la derecha las ramas desnudas de un árbol.

caption.en: The former Hanson Place Baptist Church in Brooklyn, opened in September 1860 as the city's Landmarks Preservation Commission records, the church Lowry served as pastor from 1861 to 1869, when he wrote this hymn; the tune is now usually called HANSON PLACE after it.
caption.es: La antigua Iglesia Bautista de Hanson Place, en Brooklyn, abierta en septiembre de 1860 según la Comisión de Preservación de Monumentos Históricos de la ciudad de Nueva York, la iglesia de la que Lowry fue pastor de 1861 a 1869, cuando escribió este himno; hoy la melodía suele llamarse HANSON PLACE por ella.

source: Hanson Pl SDA church jeh, photograph of the Hanson Place Seventh-day Adventist Church (formerly Hanson Place Baptist Church), 88 Hanson Place, Brooklyn, 9 January 2011 (cropped above the street)
licenceEvidence: The file's own page: source "Own work" by the uploader, who took the photograph (Nikon camera data, 9 January 2011), uploaded 16 February 2011 with the licence {{self|Cc-zero}}: "Creative Commons Zero, Public Domain Dedication". A later 2013 version by another user is a crop of the same photo. The building is identified by NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission report LP-0664 (13 October 1970): "originally erected as the Hanson Place Baptist Church ... opened in September 1860" (see rights.md).

alt.en: A printed book page with the running head "132 Sankey's Story", headed "Beautiful River", "Words by Robert Lowry" and "Music by Robert Lowry", then the lines "Shall we gather at the river Where bright angel feet have trod?" and a paragraph beginning "On a sultry afternoon in July, 1864, Dr. Lowry was sitting at his study table in Elliott Place, Brooklyn", followed by Lowry's words beginning "It is brass-band music, has a march movement".
alt.es: Una página de libro impresa con el titulillo "132 Sankey's Story" y el encabezado "Beautiful River", "Words by Robert Lowry" y "Music by Robert Lowry"; después los versos "Shall we gather at the river Where bright angel feet have trod?" y un párrafo que empieza "On a sultry afternoon in July, 1864, Dr. Lowry was sitting at his study table in Elliott Place, Brooklyn", seguido de las palabras de Lowry que empiezan "It is brass-band music, has a march movement".

caption.en: Page 132 of Ira D. Sankey's book of hymn stories (Philadelphia, 1907), the third telling: Lowry writes the words at his study table in Elliott Place, Brooklyn, then the tune at his parlour organ, and calls it "brass-band music".
caption.es: La página 132 del libro de historias de himnos de Ira D. Sankey (Filadelfia, 1907), la tercera versión: Lowry escribe la letra en la mesa de su estudio, en Elliott Place, Brooklyn, luego la melodía en el órgano de su salón, y la llama "música de banda de metales".

source: Ira D. Sankey, My Life and the Story of the Gospel Hymns and of Sacred Songs and Solos (Philadelphia: P. W. Ziegler Co., 1907), p. 132, "Beautiful River"
library: Princeton Theological Seminary Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Published Philadelphia 1907; Ira D. Sankey died 1908; the words quoted are Lowry's (died 1899). Faithful scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).
credit: Princeton Theological Seminary Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A yellowed oblong page of printed music headed "Rev. R. Lowry.", "Beautiful River." and "220". Three systems of two staves in 4/4 with three flats carry verses 1 and 2, from "Shall we gather at the river", and a section marked "CHORUS.", "Yes, we'll gather at the river", ending "That flows by the throne of God." Verses 3 to 5 are printed below in three columns, each ending "Cho. Yes, we'll gather, etc.", over the page number 153.
alt.es: Una página apaisada de música impresa, amarillenta, con el encabezado "Rev. R. Lowry.", "Beautiful River." y "220". Tres sistemas de dos pentagramas a 4/4, con tres bemoles, llevan las estrofas 1 y 2, desde "Shall we gather at the river", y una parte marcada "CHORUS.", "Yes, we'll gather at the river", que termina "That flows by the throne of God." Las estrofas 3 a 5 van debajo en tres columnas, cada una terminada en "Cho. Yes, we'll gather, etc.", sobre el número de página 153.

caption.en: "Beautiful River", No. 220 on page 153 of Happy Voices (New York: American Tract Society, 1865), the hymn's earliest known printing, credited to "Rev. R. Lowry": five verses, the last three in columns under the music.
caption.es: "Beautiful River", el n.º 220, en la página 153 de Happy Voices (Nueva York: American Tract Society, 1865), la primera impresión conocida del himno, atribuido a "Rev. R. Lowry": cinco estrofas, las tres últimas en columnas bajo la música.

source: Happy Voices: New Hymns and Tunes, with Many Popular and Sterling Old Ones, for the Home Circle and Sabbath-Schools (New York: American Tract Society, 1865), No. 220, "Beautiful River", p. 153
library: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, Music Library, Don Yoder Collection of American Hymnody (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: UNC catalogue record b68446652; Internet Archive happyvoicesnewhy00amer
licenceEvidence: Published New York 1865; the only work on the page is Lowry's (died 1899). Faithful scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).

alt.en: An oblong page of printed music headed "110", "BEAUTIFUL RIVER." and "R. L.", with the Bible verse "And he showed me a pure River of Water of Life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the Throne of God and of the Lamb." and "Rev. xxii. 1." above the music, marked "Cheerful.". Three systems of two staves in 4/4 with three flats carry verses 1 and 2 and the chorus; verses 3 to 6 are printed below in two columns. Music from the facing page shows faintly through the paper.
alt.es: Una página apaisada de música impresa con el encabezado "110", "BEAUTIFUL RIVER." y "R. L.", y sobre la música el versículo "And he showed me a pure River of Water of Life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the Throne of God and of the Lamb." y "Rev. xxii. 1.", con la indicación "Cheerful.". Tres sistemas de dos pentagramas a 4/4, con tres bemoles, llevan las estrofas 1 y 2 y el estribillo; las estrofas 3 a 6 van debajo en dos columnas. La música de la página de enfrente se transparenta un poco.

caption.en: "Beautiful River" on page 110 of Lowry's own Bright Jewels for the Sunday School (New York: Biglow & Main, 1869), signed "R. L.", with Revelation 22:1 above the music: the four parts our arrangement is read from.
caption.es: "Beautiful River" en la página 110 de Bright Jewels for the Sunday School (Nueva York: Biglow & Main, 1869), el libro del propio Lowry, firmado "R. L.", con Apocalipsis 22:1 sobre la música: las cuatro voces de las que se lee nuestro arreglo.

source: Bright Jewels for the Sunday School, Rev. Rob't Lowry, editor, assisted by Wm. F. Sherwin and Chester G. Allen (New York: Biglow & Main, 1869), "Beautiful River", p. 110
library: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, Music Library, Don Yoder Collection of American Hymnody (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: UNC catalogue record b7255697; Internet Archive brightjewelsfors00lowr_0
